sub: Named after the tribe of Quraysh in ayah 1
theme: Allah reminds Quraysh of His gifts: safe trade journeys in winter and summer, food instead of hunger, and safety instead of fear. So they should worship Him alone, the Lord of the Kaʿbah.
story: Most say it was revealed in Makkah, and “this House” points there; a minority view calls it Madinan. It is closely tied to Al-Fīl. Some early copies even wrote the two without a Bismillah between them, but the standard copy separates them.

Makkah was a barren valley with no crops, so Quraysh lived by trade: a winter caravan to Yemen and a summer caravan to Syria. Robbery on the roads was common, but tribes left them alone because they were the keepers of the Kaʿbah.

When Allah destroyed the elephant army, the Arabs respected Quraysh even more. Quraysh themselves knew the House belonged to Allah. The surah asks them to thank the Lord who gave them all this by worshipping Him alone.

sections.title: Quraysh, fed and safe on their journeys, should worship this House’s Lord
sections.meaning: Quraysh were used to their two trade journeys, in winter and summer, travelling in safety. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them when they faced hunger and made them safe from fear.
points: Quraysh’s familiar journeys of winter and summer
So let them worship the Lord of this House
He fed them against hunger, secured them from fear
sections.matters: Plenty of food and safety are among the greatest worldly blessings, and Quraysh had both because of the House. It would be deep ingratitude to enjoy the House’s benefits while refusing to worship its Lord.
sections.story: Hāshim, father of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, reportedly urged Quraysh to run the two yearly caravans, and profits were shared so the poor lived like the rich. Their link to the Kaʿbah kept them safe on roads where other caravans were robbed.
explained: Li-īlāfi Quraysh: the “for” links either back to Al-Fīl (Allah stopped the army so Quraysh could keep their journeys), or means “marvel at”, or leads into “let them worship”. Īlāf is what they had grown used to: the winter trip to Yemen and the summer trip to Syria.

Fal-yaʿbudū rabba hādhā al-bayt: let them worship the Lord of this House alone. The House is named because it was the source of their blessings, though He is Lord of everything. He fed them in a land with no crops, and kept them safe from raiders and from the elephant army.
teaches: Income and safety are gifts from Allah, not just the result of our plans.
Thank Allah for blessings by worshipping Him alone.
Enjoying Allah’s gifts while ignoring Him is ingratitude.
Whoever worships Allah is promised safety in this life and the next.
sections.hook: Īlāf comes twice: li-īlāfi (1), īlāfihim (2). Ayah 4 pairs two gifts in matching shape: aṭʿamahum min jūʿ (fed them, from hunger), āmanahum min khawf (secured them, from fear).

groups.text: Quraysh were used to travelling safely: the winter caravan and the summer caravan.
So let them worship the Lord of the Kaʿbah, who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.

1.explain: Li-īlāfi Quraysh: for Quraysh’s familiar security. It links either to Al-Fīl, since Allah stopped the army for their sake, or means “marvel at”, or leads into ayah 3.

2.explain: Their familiar two trips each year for trade: winter to warmer Yemen, summer to Syria. No one attacked them, because they were the people of Allah’s sanctuary.

3.explain: So let them single out the Lord of this House, the Kaʿbah, for worship. The House is named because it was the source of all their blessings.

4.explain: Makkah grew no crops, yet He fed them. He made them safe from raiders on the road and from the elephant army. Food and safety are among the greatest worldly gifts.
